threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the bus will come on time—locals know to check the timetable and plan for it to be late, every time.
Caught a guy trying to barter a half-eaten kebab for bus fare on the 3 last night. Driver just shook his head and laughed. Brixton at its finest.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a kid trading Pokémon cards for kebab slices at the playground. Only in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin can you find a party in an old train station, right next to a real train repair shop. It's like nightlife meets history!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by the way they instinctively know to step off the bus before the delay hits; waiting for BART is for tourists.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus today with two dogs in designer backpacks. Only in SF can you find pup fashionistas commuting in style alongside regular commuters.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is just about Gaudí. They miss the tiny, family-run bars where the real stories and local flavors simmer.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by the oversized map in their hands, especially when they stop dead in the middle of a busy carrer to check it.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still queue for the bus like it's a polite London thing, not just a suggestion. Locals just know when to assert their place.
Last night on the 109, a guy argued his vinyl collection was worth more than the bus fare. The driver just shook his head and kept driving.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a guy in a full suit, clutching a falafel wrap, hopping on the U-Bahn with a massive dog—only in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a kebab shop that serves late-night vegan döner with curry sauce – a local secret that beats the conventional options.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s from here when they can name the taco truck at 16th and Mission by the sound of the blender alone.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus today with a live saxophonist jammin' by the back door—only in the Tenderloin do you get a free concert with your commute.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all bars close at 2 AM, but real locals know the best ones stay open till sunrise, especially around Plaça del Sol.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can spot them by the way they hesitate at tram stops, clearly studying the map like it’s a treasure map. It's the telltale sign!
